Surface pinned: a recipe site or cooking app's search and save flow. Variants: actual cooking footage (kitchen videos) as the main subject, recipe-development/food-blogging business content, meal-kit unboxings, and "what I eat in a day" content do not belong.

questions.question: What items have been compiled into your grocery list?
questions.why: Reviewing the 26 categorized items on the grocery list ensures that all necessary ingredients from the recipe were captured correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to review the compiled shopping list and mentally check if you already own some of those items.

questions.question: Which ingredients should you remove from the generated shopping list?
questions.why: The grocery list displays editable fields with orange 'x' buttons next to items like honey and sea salt, letting you delete things you already have at home.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to apply their personal knowledge of their current pantry inventory to customize the final shopping list.

questions.question: Do you want to add any extra household items to your grocery list?
questions.why: The 'Add something...' input field with its autocomplete dropdowns provides a quick way to append everyday items like milk or chips to your grocery list.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent would strictly stick to the recipe's ingredients, missing the chance to anticipate and add your other routine grocery needs.

children.label: Cook from the recipe
children.note: 8.1 then 8.2; 8.3 as the steps demand; 8.4 after the meal. no keeper cooks a real meal on camera - the goal is the union of two mode tours and one logged make.

questions.question: Should you post this recipe to your Facebook timeline?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'Post to Facebook' dialog for the fluffy pancakes recipe, meaning proceeding will publish it to your social media account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether your cooking interests and saved recipes are broadcasted to your social network.

children.label: Verify the saves and settings
children.note: re-entered after every commit rather than once at the end: 9.1 after each save batch - four refresh cycles in uCtL alone. 9.2 after setup claims to have stuck. 9.3 wherever a derived number can be checked against its inputs, which the corpus almost never does.

questions.question: Did the save button actually register your action, or did it fail silently without showing a confirmation message?
questions.why: Web apps sometimes fail to process a save action due to network hiccups or expired sessions, requiring you to check for a success toast or filled-in heart icon before closing the page.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the recipe entirely because the agent assumed the click worked and navigated away before the site actually stored the data.

questions.question: Did you ensure the recipe remains saved in the meal planner?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'Recipe Removed!' toast and an 'Add to Meal Planner' button, indicating the recipe is currently not saved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to easily access the recipe later because the agent accidentally left it removed from the meal planner instead of saving it.

questions.question: Is the recipe you saved listed in the 'My Recipe Box' table?
questions.why: The screen shows the 'My Recipe Box' index, which is where you verify that the recipe was successfully added to your collection.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses confirmation that the recipe was actually saved to their collection if the agent fails to check the list.

questions.question: Are the recipes you selected successfully saved to your new board?
questions.why: Seeing the specific recipe pins like the Smoked Paprika Roast Chicken on the board confirms the save action actually worked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of visually confirming that your chosen recipes are safely stored in the correct collection.

questions.question: Did the ingredient successfully save to your shopping list?
questions.why: While the temporary banner and updated text indicate 'Cinnamon' was added, navigating to the shopping list tab verifies the item is actually there.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind that comes from visually confirming the ingredient is on your actual list before you go shopping.

questions.question: Are you viewing the correct tab to confirm the recipe was saved?
questions.why: This matters because the screen shows the Groceries tab is highlighted, not the Favorites tab where saved recipes would appear.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses confirmation that their recipe was successfully bookmarked if the agent checks the wrong section of the app.

questions.question: Was the recipe saved to the specific collection you chose, or did it default to a generic 'All Saves' folder?
questions.why: Sometimes the UI defaults to saving in a main folder rather than the specific board or menu you intended, requiring you to manually move it to keep things organized.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses their intended organization and might struggle to find the recipe later if the agent doesn't verify the exact destination folder.

questions.question: Do you need to refresh the page to see the recipes you just saved?
questions.why: The narrator notes that the saved pins didn't immediately show up on the board and required a manual page refresh to verify.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might falsely conclude the save failed and attempt to save it again or throw an error, when a simple refresh was all that was needed.

questions.question: Are your dietary restrictions, ingredient dislikes, and meal size correctly configured in the app's preferences?
questions.why: Verifying the selected menu types and allergy checkboxes ensures the app will automatically filter out unsafe or unwanted recipes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally confirming that your specific health and allergy constraints are strictly applied to your account.

questions.question: Does the total number of search results remain consistent as you scroll through the filtered list?
questions.why: The results count unexpectedly jumped from 10K+ to 24K+ while scrolling the same page, indicating the app may have dropped the applied filter or glitched.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose confidence that the agent is selecting a recipe from a list that actually adheres to your requested constraints.

questions.question: Do the cooking times of the displayed recipes actually align with the 'Quick' filter you applied?
questions.why: The screen shows a recipe taking 30 to 45 minutes even though the 'Quick' filter is active, indicating the app's categorization might not match your actual time limit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user receives a recipe that takes too long to prepare because the agent blindly trusted the app's broad filter instead of verifying the specific cooking time.

questions.question: Do the aggregate rating and the individual written review agree with each other?
questions.why: The summary shows a 4.5-star aggregate rating based on one rating, but the single written review displays 5 stars.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to spot inconsistencies in ratings that might affect their trust in the app or recipe.

questions.question: Does the rating count on the opened recipe page match the number of ratings shown on the search result card?
questions.why: The search result card displayed 170 ratings, so checking that the recipe page also shows 170 ratings confirms you opened the exact dish you intended.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty that the agent opened the correct recipe from the search results instead of accidentally clicking a different or sponsored link.

questions.question: Do the preparation and cook times on the recipe page match the total time displayed in the search results?
questions.why: The search list claimed the Chestnut truffle cake was ready in 1470 minutes, but the recipe's overview tab listed both prep and cook times as N/A.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You risk saving a recipe that violates your time constraints because the agent failed to catch the conflicting or missing time information.

questions.question: Should I expand the 'View Nutritional Info' dropdown to check the macros?
questions.why: The screen shows a collapsed 'View Nutritional Info' dropdown, meaning the actual calorie and macro values are currently hidden.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to verify if the recipe meets specific nutritional goals or constraints before saving it.

questions.question: Do the serving sizes match between the recipe app and the original blog post?
questions.why: Checking that the 24 servings listed on Yummly matches the 2 dozen on the original blog post confirms the recipe data was imported accurately.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to catch discrepancies in serving sizes or recipe yields when content is imported from an external site.

questions.question: Did you calculate the total calories for the entire dish by multiplying the servings by the calories per serving?
questions.why: The screen lists 6 servings at 434 calories each, requiring you to deduce the unstated total of 2,604 calories for the whole meatloaf.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the assurance that the agent correctly calculates unstated nutritional totals that might violate your dietary constraints.

questions.question: Do the total nutritional values in the meal planner match the sum of the individual recipes you added?
questions.why: The meal planner displayed 440 calories and 12g of fat, but the individual Moroccan tea and stew recipes only added up to 390 calories and 4.5g of fat.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses accurate dietary tracking if the agent fails to notice that the app's nutritional calculator is producing incorrect totals.

questions.question: Does the total number of saved pins match the expected count based on what you added?
questions.why: The board tile displaying 7 pins contradicts the expected total of 9, which should include the 6 original pins plus the 3 newly saved recipes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that all of their carefully selected recipes were successfully saved to the collection.

questions.question: Does the item count in the category header remain consistent between these moments?
questions.why: The 'Baking & Cooking' category header spontaneously changes from showing 3 items to 5 items without any new items being added to the list.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses an accurate understanding of how many recipes are actually saved in their collection.
